columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Founded 2002 (launched 2003); acquired by Microsoft in 2016 for USD 26B; HQ in Sunnyvale / Mountain View, California.
Hundreds of millions of members worldwide (1B+ registered; significant monthly actives, exact counts vary by source); professional identity vs recreational networks.
Profiles for individuals; Pages for companies/brands/institutions; feed posts, articles, newsletters, groups, messaging, jobs, ads, events, and learning content.
Free membership plus premium SKUs (Premium Career, Sales Navigator, Recruiter) and advertising, premium unlocks more views, InMail, filters, and analytics.

strengths.title: Professional identity and networking hub
strengths.detail: Living resume and networking platform, central for hiring, recruiting, B2B sales, and career building.

strengths.title: Content and thought leadership
strengths.detail: Posts, articles, newsletters, and events help professionals and companies build audience and authority.

strengths.title: Robust B2B advertising and targeting
strengths.detail: Ads and Pages can target by industry, role, seniority, and skills, strong for B2B marketing.

strengths.title: Company Pages and employer branding
strengths.detail: Organizations use Pages, Showcase Pages, and education pages for brand, jobs, and culture.

weaknesses.title: Feed noise and engagement quality
weaknesses.detail: Increasingly filled with generic or non-professional content, signal-to-noise can be low for thought leadership.

weaknesses.title: Premium cost and complexity
weaknesses.detail: Advanced features sit behind multiple premium SKUs that can be confusing and costly.

weaknesses.title: Limited deep community features
weaknesses.detail: Groups and events exist, but Discord, Circle, and Mighty Networks offer richer ongoing community tools.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. LinkedIn is microsoft-owned professional social network for profiles, company pages, content, jobs, messaging, and B2B advertising. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

LinkedIn is a business-oriented social media platform where professionals build profiles, connect with colleagues and companies, and share content to grow their careers and businesses. Official site.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and LinkedIn side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On LinkedIn you can use Short-form video, Courses, Newsletters, and Community & Messaging as first-class product jobs. The job is hanging out, announcements, and live conversation, not packaging knowledge into something strangers can browse later.

Using Kahana with LinkedIn

You can use both. LinkedIn keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep live conversation on LinkedIn. Pin a Kahana hub or Club link in a channel, discuss live there, and assign the next ebook, video, or course from Kahana so the syllabus is not buried in the thread.
